does: The AdvanceHintCommand (the XAML fires it 100 ms after Loaded, then every 10 s): when hints exist and translations are loaded, flips VisibileHintIndex between the two hint slots and draws a hint at random from ecl::HintManager (MSVC-style LCG rand seeded once with rand() when the view model is made, up to 100 tries), keeping only hints whose Keyboard (+0x15) or Controller (+0x14) flag fits the input method, and skipping a hint with a [binding] placeholder when no local player view model can resolve it.

evidence.says: macOS pseudo-code: seed at this+0x2fc, multiplier 0x343fd, increment 0x269ec3, modulo the HintManager count (+0x14), entry stride 0x30, tests +0x14/+0x15, scans for [ and ]
The macOS build's symbols hold this name; nothing but the name ties it to this function

dx11: the function the constructor code:gui::DCLoadingScreen::DCLoadingScreen binds into the AdvanceHintCommand (+0x358); it reads ecl::HintManager through +0x370 (count +0x14), steps the LCG 0x343fd/0x269ec3 in +0x364, indexes 0x38-byte ecl::Hint entries testing +0x15 (keyboard) or +0x14 (controller), hands the entry's Description (+4) to the slot object and writes VisibileHintIndex +0x350, as the macOS function does with its own offsets

wrapped by the fork F5 (pre/post): it runs 100 ms after the loading screen appears and every 10 s after (HintShown rows at LoadModule +7 ms, then about 9.3-10 s apart, on the first start, a level load, a return to the menu and a save's load); when it draws a hint VisibileHintIndex (+0x350) flips and the drawn index is ((LCG state +0x364 >> 16) & 0x7fff) % count of the last step
